external_entities.name: customers
external_entities.description: Customers who browse and order socks through the mobile app and receive faxed confirmations.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: Mobile application used by customers to browse and order socks.
processes.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: web API
processes.description: API used by the mobile app, storing customer information and handing orders to SIMS. The API also receives SQL statements from spreadsheet macros to change prices and product copy.
processes.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
processes.notes: Nobody here can tell me what the API does about authentication.

processes.name: SIMS
processes.description: Stock and inventory system that receives orders, writes delivery addresses to a flat file, and sends dispatch notes to the fax gateway.
processes.source_excerpt: SIMS does two things with an order.

processes.name: fax gateway
processes.description: Gateway that receives dispatch notes and faxes customer confirmations using the number stored against the order.
processes.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway, which faxes the customer a confirmation with their name and address on it.
processes.notes: The text says nobody checks that the fax arrived at the right place.

processes.name: macros
processes.description: Spreadsheet macros that send SQL statements directly to the web API to change prices and product copy.
processes.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy

data_stores.name: user database
data_stores.description: Database containing customer names, addresses, and the cards they paid with.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the user database is encrypted.

data_stores.name: flat file
data_stores.description: Flat file kept alongside SIMS containing delivery addresses only.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it — only addresses go in that file, nothing else —
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the flat file is encrypted.

data_stores.name: spreadsheet
data_stores.description: Spreadsheet containing the marketing catalogue, including prices and product copy.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet.
data_stores.notes: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

data_flows.name: browse and order
data_flows.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

data_flows.name: talks over HTTP
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app talks to the web API over HTTP — not HTTPS, it's on the list.

data_flows.name: keep customers
data_flows.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database
data_flows.data_description: customer names, addresses, and payment cards

data_flows.name: hand order
data_flows.source_excerpt: When an order is placed the API hands the order over to SIMS

data_flows.name: write address
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it

data_flows.name: send dispatch
data_flows.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway

data_flows.name: fax confirmation
data_flows.source_excerpt: which faxes the customer a confirmation with their name and address on it.
data_flows.data_description: confirmation with customer name and address

data_flows.name: change prices
data_flows.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy
data_flows.data_description: SQL statements changing prices and product copy

trust_boundaries.name: customer mobile device
trust_boundaries.description: The mobile-device context in which customers use the mobile app.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

trust_boundaries.name: office
trust_boundaries.description: Office location where the marketing laptop and spreadsheet are located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

assumptions.assumption: The mobile app is placed in a customer-controlled mobile-device trust zone.
assumptions.basis: The text says customers use the mobile app, implying it runs in the customer mobile-device context.
It contains customer names, addresses, and payment card information.
It contains delivery addresses, which are personal data.
